I have farmed these 6 mu of land in Quzhou County for over thirty years, and like my neighbors, I know the wheat-corn double cropping system is the safest way to feed my family and earn steady income. The soil here on the North China Plain is good, and with two crops a year I can make the most of it. I am 55 now and not looking to take risks with new crops like stevia or vegetables—the markets for those are too uncertain, and my back is not what it used to be. 

This year I will sow winter wheat in October and follow it with summer maize in June right after the wheat harvest. I will buy improved wheat seed (Jimai 22 or Luyuan 502) and hybrid maize seed (Denghai 605) from the local dealer, because the yields are much better than saving my own seed. For the wheat, I will rotary-till the fields before sowing and apply compound fertilizer as a base, then top-dress with urea at jointing time in spring. I will irrigate four times: at sowing, overwintering, jointing, and grain filling. For the maize, I will plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble to save labor and time during that busy June window; I will fertilize at sowing and again at the big trumpet stage, and irrigate twice. I will spray herbicide once for each crop, and keep an eye out for insects and disease—usually one or two sprays for wheat and two for corn. I expect about 1000 jin per mu of wheat and a bit more for the corn, which is what I usually get.
